task: Extend the AWS architecture diagram at /home/user/Documents/aws_arch.drawio. The file contains 3 existing shapes (VPC, EC2, RDS). Add 7 new shapes with these labels: CloudFront, LoadBalancer, Web1, Web2, App1, App2, S3Bucket. Apply fill colors: Web1 and Web2 must be #dae8fc (blue); App1 and App2 must be #d5e8d4 (green). Connect LoadBalancer to Web1. The final diagram must have exactly 10 vertices on page 0. Save the file.
task_grounding: Open the file /home/user/Documents/aws_arch.drawio in draw.io Desktop. The file already contains 3 labeled shapes: 'VPC', 'EC2', and 'RDS' (all with white fill). Extend the diagram so it becomes a full 3-tier AWS web application architecture. Add exactly 7 new shapes with these labels: 'CloudFront', 'LoadBalancer', 'Web1', 'Web2', 'App1', 'App2', 'S3Bucket'. Apply fill colors: both 'Web1' and 'Web2' must have fillColor #dae8fc (blue); both 'App1' and 'App2' must have fillColor #d5e8d4 (green). Draw a connection (arrow) from 'LoadBalancer' to 'Web1'. When finished the first page must have exactly 10 vertices total (the 3 originals plus 7 new ones). Save the file at the same path /home/user/Documents/aws_arch.drawio (Ctrl+S).

verification.prompt: Inspect the vertices list. Do the two shapes labeled 'Web1' and 'Web2' both have fillColor #dae8fc in their style string, AND do 'App1' and 'App2' both have fillColor #d5e8d4? Answer yes only if all four conditions are met.
verification.description: Web1/Web2 are blue (#dae8fc) and App1/App2 are green (#d5e8d4)

verification.prompt: Inspect the connections list. Does it include an edge whose source vertex is labeled 'LoadBalancer' and whose target vertex is labeled 'Web1'? (Cross-reference source/target IDs with the vertices.)
verification.description: Connection from LoadBalancer to Web1 exists

cli_feasibility.translation: CLI: project open <file>, shape add --type <type> --label 'text', shape list → shape style --id <id> --fill-color <#hex>, connect add --source <id> --target <id>, page add/rename, project save
